description.en: From Fairuz to the Cedars: songs, dabke, football, food and every corner of the map.
description.fr: De Fairouz aux Cèdres : chansons, dabké, foot, bonne bouffe et tous les coins du pays.
description.ar: من فيروز لرجال الأرز: غناني، دبكة، فوتبول، أكل طيّب وكل زاوية من لبنان.
description.es: De Fairuz a los Cedros: canciones, dabke, fútbol, buena mesa y cada rincón del país.

questions.text: What is the capital of Lebanon?
questions.explain: Beirut sits on a headland poking into the Mediterranean, as if it wanted a better sea view.
questions.source: [VERIFY] trivial; any encyclopedia (Britannica: Beirut)

questions.text: What is Lebanon's highest peak?
questions.explain: It rises about 3,088 m, high above the Qadisha Valley in the north.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Qurnat al-Sawdāʾ' (name, ~3,088 m, location above Qadisha)

questions.text: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within Lebanon?
questions.explain: Its source is in the Bekaa, near Baalbek.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Līṭānī River' (longest entirely within Lebanon; source near Baalbek)

questions.text: What is the Arabic name of the ancient city of Byblos?
questions.explain: Same city, two names: the Greeks said Byblos, everyone at the harbour says Jbeil.
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO WHC 'Byblos' (Byblos = Jbeil)

questions.text: What is Jeita Grotto?
questions.explain: The lower cave is visited by boat, on an underground river. Yes, a river. Inside a mountain.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Jeita Grotto official site / Britannica (limestone karst caves; lower grotto by boat)

questions.text: The famous Pigeon Rocks stand off which Beirut area?
questions.explain: The Corniche's favourite sunset spot, and its favourite selfie spot.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica / Lebanon Ministry of Tourism (Pigeon Rocks off Raouché)

questions.text: Which city is nicknamed "the Bride of the Bekaa"?
questions.explain: The Berdawni river runs through it, lined with open-air restaurants and very full tables.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Zahlé municipality / Britannica (nickname 'Bride of the Bekaa'; Berdawni river)

questions.text: The ancient "Cedars of God" forest is near which town?
questions.explain: With the Qadisha Valley, it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO WHC 'Ouadi Qadisha and the Forest of the Cedars of God' (near Bsharri)

questions.text: Saida lies north of Beirut, on the road to Byblos.
questions.explain: Head south instead: Saida is about 40 km down the coast from Beirut, on the way to Tyre.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Sidon' (port city about 40 km south of Beirut)

questions.text: Which of these ski resorts is in Lebanon?
questions.explain: The local boast: ski in the morning, swim in the sea in the afternoon.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Mzaar Kfardebian official site (location in Keserwan, Lebanon)

questions.text: The Phoenicians are famous for spreading…
questions.explain: Thank them for every text you send: Greek and Latin letters grew out of it, and so did the Arabic script, via Aramaic.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Phoenician alphabet' (ancestor of Greek, then Latin; Arabic script via Aramaic and Nabataean)

questions.text: Lebanon's Independence Day is celebrated on…
questions.explain: It goes back to 1943, and the whole country gets the day off.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Lebanese government / Britannica (Independence Day 22 November); distractor '31 August' replaced by 21 March (Mother's Day in Lebanon); Lebanese reviewer: confirm 10 March, 1 May and 21 March are neutral

questions.text: The great temples of Baalbek were built in the time of which empire?
questions.explain: The Romans called the city Heliopolis, "city of the sun".
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO WHC 'Baalbek' (Roman temples; Heliopolis)

questions.text: Which god's temple at Baalbek is one of the best-preserved Roman temples anywhere?
questions.explain: It stands next to the six giant columns left from the Temple of Jupiter.
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO WHC 'Baalbek' / Britannica (Temple of Bacchus preservation; beside the Temple of Jupiter columns)

questions.text: Ancient Tyre was famous for which precious dye?
questions.explain: It came from murex sea snails, and cost so much that purple became the colour of emperors.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Tyrian purple' (murex sea snails; imperial/royal purple)

questions.text: Byblos is considered one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
questions.explain: UNESCO notes traces of settlement there from Neolithic times.
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO WHC 'Byblos' ('continuously inhabited since Neolithic times')

questions.text: Who wrote "The Prophet"?
questions.explain: Published in 1923, it has been translated into dozens of languages.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Khalil Gibran' (The Prophet, 1923; translations claim)

questions.text: Gibran Khalil Gibran was born in which town?
questions.explain: A museum in Bsharri holds his paintings, and he rests there.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Gibran Museum, Bsharri (birthplace; museum and resting place)

questions.text: Amin Maalouf won France's Prix Goncourt for which novel?
questions.explain: He won it in 1993. In 2023 he became Perpetual Secretary of the Académie française.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Académie Goncourt laureates (1993, Le Rocher de Tanios); Académie française (Maalouf, secrétaire perpétuel 2023)

questions.text: In Lebanon, who is "Teta"?
questions.explain: And grandpa? "Jeddo". Both will tell you you've lost weight and must eat something.
questions.source: [VERIFY] common Lebanese usage (reviewer)

questions.text: What do Lebanese people call backgammon?
questions.explain: A roll of six and five has its own name: "shesh besh".
questions.source: [VERIFY] tawleh = backgammon; 'shesh besh' = a roll of six and five (Persian/Turkish numbers)

questions.text: A classic Lebanese greeting mixes three languages: "Hi, kifak, ça va?"
questions.explain: Bonus points if the sentence ends with "merci, yalla bye".
questions.source: [VERIFY] widely cited Lebanese code-switching phrase (keep as culture, not a statistic)

questions.text: What is Lebanese "zajal"?
questions.explain: Lebanese zajal is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list.
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO ICH 'Al-Zajal, recited or sung poetry' (Lebanon, 2014)

questions.text: The Baalbek International Festival, held in the Roman temples, was founded in the 1950s.
questions.explain: Fairuz and the Rahbani brothers performed there in its early years.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Baalbeck International Festival official site (founded 1956; early Rahbani/Fairuz nights)

questions.text: Which Hollywood actor was born in Beirut?
questions.explain: His family moved when he was small and he grew up mostly in Toronto. Still counts.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Keanu Reeves' (born Beirut 1964; raised mainly in Toronto)

questions.text: What is Fairuz's real name?
questions.explain: Jeanette Feghali is the real name of Sabah.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Fairuz' (Nouhad Haddad); Britannica 'Sabah' (Jeanette Feghali)

questions.text: Fairuz's most famous collaborators were…
questions.explain: Assi Rahbani was also her husband. The Bee Gees were busy.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Fairuz' (Assi and Mansour Rahbani; married Assi)

questions.text: Fairuz's song "Li Beirut" uses the melody of which classical piece?
questions.explain: The concerto is by Spanish composer Joaquín Rodrigo.
questions.source: [VERIFY] song credits 'Li Beirut' (melody: Rodrigo, Concierto de Aranjuez, 2nd mvt)

questions.text: Which legendary singer was nicknamed "Al-Shahrourah" (the blackbird)?
questions.explain: She also starred in dozens of Egyptian and Lebanese films.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Sabah' (nickname al-Shahrourah; film career)

questions.text: Which instrument does Lebanese-French star Ibrahim Maalouf play?
questions.explain: He plays a quarter-tone trumpet that can play Arabic scales.
questions.source: [VERIFY] ibrahimmaalouf.com bio (trumpet; quarter-tone trumpet)

questions.text: Which Beirut-born pop star had a hit with "Grace Kelly"?
questions.explain: He moved to Paris as a child, then to London.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica / official bio 'Mika' (born Beirut 1983; Paris then London; 'Grace Kelly' 2007)

questions.text: What is an oud?
questions.explain: The European lute takes its name from it.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'ʿūd' (fretless; name 'the wood'; root of the word 'lute')

questions.text: Which of these songs was a 2000s hit for Nancy Ajram?
questions.explain: It came out in 2004 and played all summer long, including in your aunt's car.
questions.source: [VERIFY] album credits 'Ah W Noss' (Nancy Ajram, 2004); distractors by other artists

questions.text: What is dabke?
questions.explain: Its name comes from the stamping of feet on the ground.
questions.source: [VERIFY] trivial; Britannica 'dabke' (name linked to stamping)

questions.text: The leader at the head of a dabke line often waves a…
questions.explain: The leader improvises steps while the line keeps the base rhythm.
questions.source: [VERIFY] folk-dance references (handkerchief/mandil of the line leader); reviewer: «محرمة»

questions.text: Which Lebanese dance company is famous for mixing dabke with modern dance?
questions.explain: It was founded by Abdel-Halim Caracalla.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Caracalla Dance Theatre official site (founder Abdel-Halim Caracalla)

questions.text: Which instrument traditionally leads village dabke music?
questions.explain: Players breathe in through the nose while blowing, so the sound never stops.
questions.source: [VERIFY] ethnomusicology refs on the mijwiz (dabke; circular breathing); AR term for bagpipe [native review]

questions.text: Dabke is traditionally danced solo: one dancer, no line.
questions.explain: It's a line or a circle, hands or shoulders linked. Nobody does dabke alone.
questions.source: [VERIFY] trivial

questions.text: At a Lebanese wedding, the joyful procession of drums, singing and dancing that welcomes the couple is the…
questions.explain: Guests often add the zalghouta, the joyful ululation.
questions.source: [VERIFY] wedding-custom references (zaffeh; zalghouta = ululation)

questions.text: What is the nickname of Lebanon's national football team?
questions.explain: The cedar is also at the centre of the national flag.
questions.source: [VERIFY] FIFA / Lebanese FA (team nickname; AR «رجال الأرز»)

questions.text: In which year did Lebanon host the AFC Asian Cup?
questions.explain: Japan won that edition.
questions.source: [VERIFY] AFC 'AFC Asian Cup 2000' (host Lebanon; winner Japan)

questions.text: Lebanese midfielder Roda Antar played in the top league of which country?
questions.explain: He played for Hamburg, Freiburg and Cologne.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Transfermarkt / Kicker 'Roda Antar' (Hamburger SV, SC Freiburg, 1. FC Köln)

questions.text: In which sport has Lebanon's national team played at several World Cups?
questions.explain: Lebanon also hosted the FIBA Asia Cup in 2017.
questions.source: [VERIFY] FIBA archive (World Cup 2002, 2006, 2010, 2023; FIBA Asia Cup 2017 hosted by Lebanon)

questions.text: Which club has won the most Lebanese Premier League titles?
questions.explain: Al-Ansar once won eleven league titles in a row.
questions.source: [VERIFY] RSSSF 'Lebanon - List of Champions' (record holder Al-Ansar; 11 straight titles from 1988; Safa far behind); Lebanese reviewer: confirm the club list (Al-Ahed dropped: party affiliation, and its title count nears the record)

questions.text: At the 2023 AFC Asian Cup, Lebanon played the opening match against which host nation?
questions.explain: The tournament kicked off at Lusail Stadium, the very ground of the 2022 World Cup final.
questions.source: [VERIFY] AFC match report: Qatar 3-0 Lebanon, 12 January 2024, Lusail Stadium (AFC Asian Cup 2023 opening match)

questions.text: Lebanon first qualified for the Asian Cup through qualifiers (not as host) for which edition?
questions.explain: That tournament was held in the United Arab Emirates.
questions.source: [VERIFY] AFC 'AFC Asian Cup 2019' (Lebanon's first qualification via qualifiers; hosted by UAE)

questions.text: What is the main ingredient of tabbouleh?
questions.explain: The bulgur is just a sprinkle: parsley is the star. A bowl of bulgur with a bit of green is not tabbouleh.
questions.source: [VERIFY] cookbook/encyclopedia 'tabbouleh' (parsley-based Lebanese version)

questions.text: What is toum?
questions.explain: Garlic, oil, lemon, salt, and not a single egg. Your breath will remember it tomorrow.
questions.source: [VERIFY] cookbook refs 'toum' (garlic, oil, lemon, salt; no egg)

questions.text: What gives sfouf cake its yellow colour?
questions.explain: It's a semolina cake, often topped with pine nuts or almonds.
questions.source: [VERIFY] cookbook refs 'sfouf' (turmeric, semolina; AR «عقدة صفرا»)

questions.text: How is kibbeh nayyeh served?
questions.explain: It comes with fresh mint, onion and a drizzle of olive oil.
questions.source: [VERIFY] cookbook refs 'kibbeh nayyeh' (raw meat + fine bulgur); AR options differ on purpose (name says 'raw')

questions.text: Which salad is topped with crunchy toasted or fried bread?
questions.explain: Sumac gives its dressing a tangy, reddish tint.
questions.source: [VERIFY] trivial; cookbook refs 'fattoush' (sumac dressing)

questions.text: Who directed the films "Caramel" and "Capernaum"?
questions.explain: She also acts in her own films.
questions.source: [VERIFY] IMDb / Britannica 'Nadine Labaki' (director and actress of Caramel, Capernaum)

questions.text: Which award did "Capernaum" win at the 2018 Cannes Film Festival?
questions.explain: It went on to an Oscar nomination for Best Foreign Language Film.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Festival de Cannes palmarès 2018 (Prix du jury: Capharnaüm); 91st Academy Awards (2019) nominee, Best Foreign Language Film

questions.text: Which Hollywood star's father is of Lebanese descent?
questions.explain: Her father's family came from Lebanon; she was born in Mexico.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Salma Hayek' (father of Lebanese descent; born Mexico)

questions.text: What was "Studio El Fan"?
questions.explain: Many famous Lebanese singers got their start there.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Télé Liban / press archives 'Studio El Fan' (Simon Asmar, launched 1970s)

questions.text: Shakira's Lebanese roots are on her mother's side.
questions.explain: They come from her father's side. Hips don't lie, and neither does this answer.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Shakira' (paternal Lebanese ancestry)

questions.text: Tyre's UNESCO-listed site includes one of the largest Roman…
questions.explain: Its stands could seat around 20,000 chariot-race fans.
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO WHC 'Tyre' (Roman hippodrome; size/seating claim)

questions.text: The ruined city of Anjar in the Bekaa dates from which dynasty?
questions.explain: Its grid of streets, arches and shops was laid out in the early 700s.
questions.source: [VERIFY] UNESCO WHC 'Anjar' (Umayyad, early 8th century); reviewer: dynasty name OK under §11.2

questions.text: Which palace in the Chouf hosts a famous summer festival?
questions.explain: Its courtyards turn into an open-air stage every summer.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Beiteddine Art Festival official site (Beiteddine palace, Chouf)

questions.text: The Shouf Biosphere Reserve is famous for its…
questions.explain: It protects about a quarter of Lebanon's remaining cedar forests.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Shouf Biosphere Reserve official site / UNESCO MAB (cedar share claim ~25%)

questions.text: Which river rises in the northern Bekaa and flows north out of Lebanon?
questions.explain: Locals call it al-Assi, "the rebel", because it flows north.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Orontes River' (source near Hermel; flows north; 'al-Assi' = the rebel)

questions.text: The Sea Castle is a landmark of which city?
questions.explain: It sits on a small island linked to the shore by a stone causeway.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Lebanon Ministry of Tourism 'Sidon Sea Castle' (island + causeway)

questions.text: What does "yalla" mean?
questions.explain: It also ends every Lebanese phone call: "yalla bye".
questions.source: [VERIFY] trivial; common usage ('yalla bye')

questions.text: Za'atar on a man'oushe is mainly a blend of thyme, sumac and…
questions.explain: Man'oushe is the classic breakfast, straight from the bakery oven.
questions.source: [VERIFY] cookbook refs 'za'atar' blend (thyme, sumac, sesame)

questions.text: What tree is in the centre of the Lebanese flag?
questions.explain: The green cedar sits on a white band between two red bands.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Lebanese Constitution art. 5 / Britannica 'flag of Lebanon'

questions.text: Which northern coastal town is famous for its fresh lemonade?
questions.explain: Batroun also claims to be one of the oldest towns on the coast.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Lebanon Ministry of Tourism / travel guides (Batroun lemonade; 'one of the oldest coastal towns')

questions.text: Tripoli's old souks are famous for which handmade craft, sold in fragrant bars?
questions.explain: The city's Khan al-Saboun, the soap khan, is centuries old.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Khan al-Saboun, Tripoli (soap khan; olive-oil soap craft)

questions.text: Sea turtles come to nest on the beaches of the Tyre Coast Nature Reserve.
questions.explain: Loggerhead and green turtles lay their eggs in the sand there.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Tyre Coast Nature Reserve (loggerhead and green turtle nesting)

questions.text: Which southern mountain town is famous for its tall waterfall?
questions.explain: It's also known for handmade knives with bird-shaped handles.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Jezzine municipality / Ministry of Tourism (waterfall; bird-handled cutlery craft)

questions.text: What ancient monument stands alone on a hill near Hermel?
questions.explain: Locals call it Qamouaa el-Hermel; it is about 2,000 years old.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Lebanon DGA / archaeology refs 'Qamouaa el-Hermel' (pyramid-topped tower, ~1st c. BC)

questions.text: The late composer and playwright Ziad Rahbani was the son of which singer?
questions.explain: His father was Assi Rahbani. Ziad turned the family music into sharp, very funny theatre.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Britannica 'Fairuz' / 'Ziad Rahbani' (son of Fairuz and Assi Rahbani; died July 2025)

questions.text: Which singer was known as "the Voice of Lebanon"?
questions.explain: He kept singing for more than sixty years.
questions.source: [VERIFY] press obituaries 2013 'Wadih El Safi' (nickname 'the Voice of Lebanon'; career length)

questions.text: The Sursock Museum, a modern art museum in a white villa, is in which Beirut area?
questions.explain: The villa mixes Venetian and Ottoman styles.
questions.source: [VERIFY] Sursock Museum official site (Achrafieh; modern and contemporary art)

questions.text: Who is the all-time top scorer of Lebanon's national football team?
questions.explain: He wore the captain's armband at the 2019 Asian Cup, the first the Cedars reached through qualifying.
questions.source: [VERIFY] RSSSF / national-team records (Hassan Maatouk all-time top scorer, tally as of 2024); AFC Asian Cup 2019 squad (captain; first qualification on the pitch, 2000 was as host)

questions.text: For breakfast, knefeh is often stuffed inside a…
questions.explain: Cheese, semolina, syrup and sesame bread: the sweetest way to start a day.
questions.source: [VERIFY] food refs 'knefeh / ka'ak' (Lebanese breakfast)
